key_insight: ST-VTD learns shared and subject-specific spatiotemporal structure by combining a low-rank tensor model for spatial maps with an LSTM-based prior for temporal dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers an interpretable, parameter-efficient framework for multisubject data analysis, especially useful in neuroimaging and other spatiotemporal sensing applications.
method: Variational tensor factorization with structured priors for joint spatial-temporal representation
LL1-inspired low-rank regularization on spatial factors
Amortized inference via unrolled optimization, initialized with group ICA warm-start
evidence_signal: On a realistic synthetic fMRI dataset, the method reportedly outperformed representative classical and probabilistic decomposition baselines in latent factor recovery.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the warm-start and the added complexity of learning an LSTM prior, which could affect robustness on noisier real-world data.
paper_title: Variational Low-rank Tensor Decomposition for Multisubject Spatiotemporal Data Analysis
